name: Agent Dev Kit Dashboard
tag: A visual guide that helps your team plan an agent's memory, knowledge, guardrails and handoffs.

scenarios.title: Plan a customer-service agent
scenarios.ask: Plan a support agent for {tickets} tickets a day using {docs} help articles, with {guard} guardrails.
steps: Memory
Short-term memory for the current chat. Long-term notes per customer, kept 90 days.
Knowledge
Index {docs} articles into about {=docs * 6} passages for retrieval.
Guardrails
{guard} level: {=guard * 3 + 2} checks, including no refunds without approval and no personal data in replies.
Delegation
Billing and outage questions hand off to specialist agents. Angry customers go to a person.
Distribution
Plan for {=max(1, ceil(tickets / 1500))} agent instances behind one queue.
followups: Why do stricter guardrails send more to people?
Each extra check is another reason to stop and ask. That is the trade: fewer mistakes, more human work. The dashboard shows the count so you can choose.
Is this code or a diagram?
Both. The dashboard draws the architecture and exports a starter config for the Agent Development Kit that matches it.

scenarios.title: Teach agent concepts to new hires
scenarios.ask: Walk {people} new engineers through the five building blocks in {sessions} short sessions.
steps: Curriculum
Grouped memory, knowledge, guardrails, delegation and distribution into {sessions} sessions.
Visual walkthrough
Each block has an animated diagram that shows data moving through it.
Exercises
Added {=sessions * 2} build-it-yourself exercises using the sample agent.
Check-in
Short quiz at the end of each session to spot gaps.
followups: It covers the ideas but leaves little hands-on time. Three sessions is the usual sweet spot for engineers new to agents.
Can we add our own examples?
Yes. Swap in your own sample agent and the diagrams update to match it.

scenarios.title: Review an existing agent
scenarios.ask: Review our current agent: {tools} tools, {prompt_k}k-token system prompt. Where are the weak spots?
steps: Mapper
Placed your agent on the five-block map. Memory and knowledge are mixed into one prompt.
Knowledge check
About {=round(prompt_k * 0.6, 1)}k tokens of the prompt are reference text that could move to retrieval.
Delegation check
{tools} tools on one agent. Suggested splitting into {=max(1, ceil(tools / 8))} agents with focused toolsets.
Guardrail check
No output check before replies reach customers. Flagged as high priority.

result.title: Review findings
rows: Prompt tokens to move to retrieval

followups: Models choose tools less reliably as the list grows. Smaller, focused toolsets usually mean fewer wrong calls.
No. It is an estimate based on shorter prompts. Measure before and after on your own traffic.
